notes.claim: The fighting that broke out in April 2023 was triggered by a preemptive strike by the RSF.
notes.context: The SAF and RSF originally shared governance during the transitional period following the collapse of the al-Bashir regime in 2019, but tensions escalated over unified military command, leading to armed conflict on April 15, 2023. The two sides disagree on who struck first.
notes.verdict: Circumstances of conflict origin disputed (international verification has been difficult)

sources.title: Sudan Conflict Overview — International Crisis Group

notes.claim: The RSF has committed acts amounting to genocide in Darfur.
notes.context: The UN and human rights organizations have reported that the RSF has carried out mass killings, sexual violence, and forced displacement targeting non-Arab minorities in Darfur (such as the Masalit). The United States officially designated these actions as genocide in 2024.
notes.verdict: Fact (U.S. officially designated as genocide; documented by UN human rights bodies)

sources.title: UN Human Rights Council Reports on Sudan

notes.claim: Chinese-made weapons have been supplied to the RSF.
notes.context: In 2025, Chinese-made drones and guided bombs were confirmed to have been used on the RSF side, prompting the Sudanese government to demand an explanation from Beijing. China has denied any relationship with the RSF, but the details of the supply routes remain unclear.

sources.title: Chinese Weapons in Sudan's Civil War — ADF Magazine

notes.claim: RSF leader Hemedti received a death sentence from a Sudanese court in July 2026.
notes.context: A Sudanese court sentenced Hemedti and 15 associates to death in absentia on charges of war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide. The RSF claims the verdict is invalid.
notes.verdict: Fact (in absentia trial; RSF disputes the verdict)

sources.title: Sudan Court Sentences RSF Leader to Death — AP News

notes.claim: The Sudan civil war is one of the largest humanitarian crises of the 21st century.
notes.context: As of 2026, millions have been displaced internally, and the number of refugees who have fled to neighboring countries such as Chad, South Sudan, and Egypt has surged dramatically. Severe shortages of food, medical care, and shelter continue, and the United Nations has called for emergency assistance.
notes.verdict: Fact (designated as largest crisis by UN OCHA and WFP)

sources.title: Sudan Humanitarian Crisis — UN OCHA
sources.publisher: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

notes.claim: The UN Security Council has been unable to adopt a binding resolution on the Sudan civil war, limiting its response to statements.
notes.context: In response to the Sudan civil war (2023–), the UN Security Council issued multiple press statements in 2023–2024, but permanent member opposition and abstentions (particularly Russia and China) have prevented the adoption of any binding resolution with sanctions or enforcement measures. Non-binding resolutions demanding humanitarian access (such as S/RES/2724) were adopted but poorly implemented. Deployment of a UN peacekeeping force was also discussed in 2024 but no agreement was reached. International NGOs have repeatedly criticized this Security Council dysfunction as deepening the humanitarian crisis.
notes.verdict: No binding Security Council resolution (statements and non-binding resolutions only)
